To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the discursive construction of the desiring user by location-based social networking applications for gay men, such as Grindr and Scruff, clashes with the lived reality and experiences of gay, bisexual, queer, and other men who have sex with men in rural areas.

(1) The design of Grindr and Scruff, location-based networking apps for gay, bisexual and queer men, constructs the desiring user, a user whose sexuality is mediated through technology in particular ways; and (2) This desiring user clashes with the lived experiences of rural users, who experience their sexuality as more fluid and complex than the apps allow.

(1) the desiring user is a construct that emerges from the design of social computing technologies; (2) the desiring users of Grindr and Scruff are constructed as urban; and (3) the rural users of these applications do not fit the desiring user construct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways that Grindr and SCRUF construct the user as desiring, and in turn, how the users of these applications construct themselves as desiring.
how the discursive production of the desiring user in location-based social networking applications can be understood in terms of rural, queer, and sexual subjectivities.
how technology mediates the production of the user and the user’s desires.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the discursive construction of the desiring user by Grindr and SCRUF is not only at odds with the lived realities of our rural inter-locutors but also with a growing body of research that shows the diversity of gay, bisexual, queer, and trans men’s sexualities.
our findings show the ways in which the discourses of Grindr and Scruff, and the design of the applications themselves, construct the user in a particular way.

the desiring user is a discursive construction that is not only shaped through the design of location-based social networking applications, but that also is produced through the discursive practices of the application creators, the users themselves, and the researchers who study them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in how technology is used in rural areas to construct and mediate sexual subjectivities.
Grindr and SCRUF are designed to construct a desiring user, and that this user is a particular kind of gay man.
we show how discourses of sexuality and rurality are constructed in Grindr and SCRUF and how those constructions are challenged by our rural participants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while location-based social networks are designed to facilitate sexual encounters, they also produce particular sexual subjectivities and desires.
the design of location-based networking applications is informed by particular discursive constructions of sexual identity and rural life.
the desiring user is a discursively constructed figure that does not always align with the lived experience of rural gay men, who are often marginalized by both the rural and urban gay communities.
